This judgment is the outcome of the final report filed by the PI of Halsuru Gate Police Station,
Bengaluru against the accused for the offences punishable U/s. 419, 420, 468 and 471 of Indian Penal Code.

2. Brief Facts Of The Case Of Prosecution:-

The case of prosecution is that the accused is working as a Superintendent in the office of the Deputy Director (Sports Scheme) on the 1st Floor of the State Youth Center Building, Nrupathunga Road, within the limits of Halasuru Gate Police Station.
The accused was appointed by CW.13 to distribute allowances to the athletes representing the State in the Khelo India Games held in the year 2016-17.

It is alleged that the accused used the allowance of Rs. 6,370/- which was to be given to the badminton players CW.3 to CW.8 in total Rs.25,480/- for his own use, forged the signatures of CW.3 to CW.8 in the money receipt list and the accused forged signatures and false statements in the money receipt list.

It is further alleged that the accused dishonestly used the forged signatures as genuine for the purpose of defrauding the receipt C.C. No.23254/2021 list and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 468 and 471 of Indian Penal Code.
3.
In response to court summons the accused appeared through his counsel Sri. J.K.L and has been enlarged on bail.
Cognizance was taken for the alleged offences.
The prosecution papers have been furnished to the accused through his counsel as contemplated U/s 207 Cr.P.C. Heard before framing of Charges.
Charges were framed, read over and explained to the accused in Kannada language known to him, having understood the same he pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried.
4. As per the charge sheet the prosecution has cited 21 witnesses.
Out of these witnesses the prosecution has examined 9 witness as PW-1 to PW.9 and Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-11 are marked. CW.2, 4, 7 to 10, 12, 14, 17 and CW.20 are not examined by the prosecution.
5. Statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded and incriminating evidence in the case of prosecution C.C. No.23254/2021 was read over to the accused.
The accused has denied the incriminating evidence against him and submitted that, he has no defense evidence.

6. Heard arguments of learned APP for the prosecution and learned counsel for the accused.
Perused the entire materials on record.
7.

On the basis of the materials on record the following points arise for the consideration:-
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that accused being the Superintendent in the office of the Deputy Director (Sports Scheme) deputed to give allowances to the athletes representing the State in the Khelo India Games held in the year 2016-17 used the allowance of Rs.
6,370/- which was to be given to the badminton players CW.3 to CW.8 in total Rs.25,480/- for his own use, forged the signatures of CW.3 to CW.8 in the money receipt list and the accused forged signatures and false statements in the money receipt list and cheated the CW.3 to CW.8 and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 468 of Indian Penal Code ?

No.23254/2021 signatures and false statements in the money receipt list and dishonestly used the forged signatures as genuine for the purpose of defrauding the receipt list and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section 471 of Indian Penal Code.
3. What order?
8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 and 2 :- In the Negative Point No.3 :- As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9. Reasoning On Point No.1 And 2 :- The offences alleged against the accused is punishable under Sections 419, 420, 468 and 471 of Indian Penal Code.
Sec.419. Punishment for cheating by personation.-- Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Sec-420. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.--Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Sec.468. Forgery for purpose of cheating.--Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
C.C. No.23254/2021 Sec. 471. Using as genuine a forged document or electronic record.-- Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any document or electronic record which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged document or electronic record, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document or electronic record.

The Hon'ble High Court heard the State Government and ordered that a match to be played between the children who had merit among the children who had already been selected.
Accordingly the match was held and the children who had merit won the badminton match, in which his daughter also won.
He has further deposed that after this, the children who had merit played a match against children from other states.

When the Government did not give the money, they had filed an C.C. No.23254/2021 application under RTI.

So he came to know that injustice has been done to all the children.
Therefore he has filed this complaint.
His daughter was supposed to get Rs. 6000/- as a small amount.

He has further deposed that after a few days of filing the complaint, the police called him for a panchanama.

He has deposed that in 2016 the National Games of India were held at Hyderabad.
As per the orders of the Hon'ble High Court, the final selection trial was held in Hyderabad.

21. The prosecution has produced Exh.P-1 to Exh.P- 11.

Exh.P-1 is the spot mahazar, Exh.P-2 is the complaint, Exh.P- 3 is the seizure mahazar, Exh.P-5 is the FSL report, Exh.P-7 to Ex.P.-9 are the notices, Exh.P-10 is the reply to notice, Exh.P- 11 is the endorsement and Ex.D-1 is the order passed in W.P. No.4312-316/2017 of Hon'ble High Court.
Due to oversight the Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.6 are not marked serial wise.

22. It is undisputed that the accused is working as a Superintendent in the office of the Deputy Director (Sports Scheme) on the 1st Floor of the State Youth Center Building, Nrupathunga Road,
within the limits of Halasuru Gate Police Station.
It is undisputed that the accused was appointed by CW.13 to distribute allowances to the athletes representing the State in the Khelo India Games held in the year 2016-17.

The perusal of the complaint shows that the complainant in its C.C.
No.23254/2021 complaint dated 14.07.2018 had mentioned about the order passed in W.P.
No.4316/2017 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The complaint itself shows that there was an order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

Under such circumstances when there was already an order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it was incumbent upon the Investigation Officer to first go through the order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Though there was an order, the Investigating Officer has not made any efforts to get the copy of order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

the copy of an order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P. No.4312-316/2017 and 4386-391/2017 dated 02.04.2019 wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has dismissed the Nagaraj M.G vs Harising Rathod on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185103039/

23. It is allegations made by the prosecution that an amount of Rs.6,327/- was to be given to the CW.3 to CW.8 each.
In the cross-examination the PW.1 being the complainant has stated that he do not have knowledge about the paper publication.

He admits that, he had filed W.P. C.C.
No.23254/2021 No.4312/2017 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and in total 11 writ petitions were filed.

He admits that in the writ petitions it was ordered that 11 players would participate in the state level competition and the said 11 children had to go to Hyderabad in their own expenses and if the said 11 players won then only allowance would be given to them.
He admits that in the writ petitions it was ordered that paying allowance to the players would be at the discretion of the institution.
He admits that he do not know when they went to Hyderabad and when the match was conducted.
He further admits that, the writ petitioners competed against already selected players.
He further admits that among the writ petitioners 5 candidates won.
He admits that the 5 writ petitioners were provided with kits.
He admits that, the signature of the players were taken when the sports kits was distributed to them.
The PW.2 in his cross-examination has stated that he is the friend of CW.1 and therefore he has signed to Ex.P.1.
The PW.3 is the player who participated in the match.
In his cross-examination he has stated that he do not remember if he had participants in the badminton tournament held the district level.
He admits that he has filed writ petition C.C. No.23254/2021 before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and as per orders he participated in the Khelo India match.
He do not know what was the order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
He admits that Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka had given the discretion to the institution about giving allowance to the players.
He admits that all the facilities including food accommodation in Hyderabad was done by the institution and even sports kits were provided by the institution.
He admits that he has signed when the sports kits were given to him.
He admits that the institution has not caused any lost to him.
CW.9 is the officer from the treasury Bengaluru.
In the cross-examination he admits that Rs.6370/- was the total amount of allowance for a player including railway ticket charges and also sports kits.
He admits that as per the orders of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it was not mandatory to give allowance to the players.
He admits that the 4 writ petitioners who won in Hyderabad were given sports kits.
He admits that the 4 writ petitioners who played in Hyderabad were not given traveling allowance and also daily allowance.
He admits that he had participated in the said match and further admits that prior to distributing kits the signature of the players was taken.
He C.C. No.23254/2021 admits that Rs.6370/- includes traveling allowance, daily allowance and sports kits and also included traveling allowance.
He further admits that, there was no such order that the 4 writ petitioners were to be given amount in cash.
He admits that in Hyderabad they had taken signature of the players for giving the sports kits, traveling allowance.
He also admits that as against the signature of the players amount was also mentioned.
He admits that there was no any departmental enquiry against the accused.
He admits that the coach Arun had also participated in the match.
He admits that the kits were distributed in his presence.
He admits that the accused has not misused the money of the institutions.

25. The investigating officer PW-6 in his cross- examination has stated that he has obtained the statement of CW- 7 as he has also told that there is a forgery but he has not issued any notice to CW- 7.
he admits that though I Exh.P-1 it was mentioned about writ petition but he has not verified about the same and not enquired about writ petition with the CW-1.
He admits that he has not conducted mahazar in the place where khelo India match was held at Hyderabad.

He admits that CW- 3 is the mahazar witness in this case and states that signature of CW- 4 is forged.
He explains that the CW-1 has not told him that the incident occurred in Hyderabad and that he do not know that the incident took place at Hyderabad.
He admits that he has not enquired about the daily allowance and traveling allowance.
He has further stated that he had no knowledge about any orders passed by C.C. No.23254/2021 the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka.
He has stated that on the basis of report submitted by CW.13, he had filed charge sheet against the accused for the alleged offences.
He admits that had no knowledge about the writ petition submitted with regard to Khelo India match.
He admits that in the complaint there is mention of order passed in writ petition.
He admits that after 3 years of the registration of the FIR, he had conduced mahazar.

26. The PW.7 in his cross-examination has stated that though he had called the CW.1, but he has not cooperated for the investigation and further admits that after 3 years of FIR, he has conducted mahazar.

He admits that he has not issued any notice to CW.1.
27.
The version of PW.6 is that he has submitted charge sheet against the accused based on the report given by CW.13.
CW.13 is Sathith L Sajjanar who is examined as PW.9.
The PW.9 admits that there was no fault of the accused.

As per the admission given by the Investigating Officer and the documents shows that after 3 years of registration of the FIR, mahazar was conducted and the delay of 3 years in conducting the mahazar is not explained by the Investigating Officer.

The Investigating Officer has not made any efforts to go through the orders passed by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka and also has not verified the veracity of the case prior to filing the charge sheet.
As per Ex.P.10 the Harisingh Rahod was the superintendent of the institution and he had the responsibility of giving allowance to the participants players.
Even Ex.P.10
the name of one B.N. Sudhakar is mentioned but the Investigating Officer has not examined the said B.N. Sudhakar and has also not taken his statement.
Though mahazar was conducted, but it was not conducted soon after the incident and was not conducted in the place of incident.

The admission given by the PW.6 the Investigating Officer Thimmarayappa clearly shows that no proper investigation was conducted and no proper statement of witnesses was recorded prior to filing of charge sheet.

Only on the basis of report submitted by the CW.13 which is at Ex.P.10, charge sheet is filed against the accused without C.C. No.23254/2021 Nagaraj M.G vs Harising Rathod on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185103039/
8 conducting proper investigation.

sentences.text: The admission given by the PW.9 itself shows that there was no forgery was committed by the accused.
Had if the Investigating Officer had recorded the statement of B.N. Sudhakar and had if the CW.4 to CW.8 were enquired properly, the Investigation would have ben proper.

On the basis of Ex.P.10 which shows that accused was superintendent of the Institutions and he had the responsibility of giving allowance to the participants players does not conclusively establish that the accused has committed alleged offences.
28. The entire case of the prosecution is based on the ground that the accused forged the signature of the players and used money for his own use.
There are no materials to prove that accused forged the signature of the players and used money for his own use.
In the absence of cogent evidence the charges levelled against the accused is not proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
29. Thus in the absence of cogent oral and documentary evidence the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the alleged C.C. No.23254/2021 offenses against the accused.
Hence Point No.1 and 2 are answered in NEGATIVE.

30. Point No. 3:- For the aforesaid reasons, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/s.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused is hereby Acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.419, 420, 468 and 471 of Indian Penal Code.
The cash security deposited by the accused for his release on bail shall be refunded on proper identification.

Sec.419. Punishment for cheating by personation.-- Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Sec-420. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.--Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Sec.468. Forgery for purpose of cheating.--Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Using as genuine a forged document or electronic record.-- Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any document or electronic record which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged document or electronic record, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document or electronic record.
